title: Enable guided meditation ambient sounds to stream from internet URLs

requirements.text: Update the Guided Meditation ambient sound selector to support streaming audio from full internet URLs (in addition to existing bundled local assets), so selecting a sound plays that URL directly.

quotes: MAKE FINAL YOU CAN ADDD SOME AUDIO FROM THE INTERNET

acceptanceCriteria: In Guided Meditation, ambient sound options can include full https:// URLs and are played successfully when selected.
Existing local ambient sound options (e.g., /assets/guided-meditation/*.mp3) continue to work without changes.
If a selected remote audio URL fails to load or play, the page shows a clear English error message and does not crash or get stuck in a playing state.

requirements.text: Implement the Guided Meditation audio loading logic so it uses the selected option value as the audio source directly (rather than assuming a local asset base path), while keeping the rest of the Guided Meditation experience unchanged (timer, breathing visual, script, and navigation).

quotes: You want the final version of your page with audio loaded directly from the internet.

acceptanceCriteria: Changing the selected ambient sound while audio is playing switches playback to the newly selected source (local or remote) without requiring a page refresh.
Starting/pausing/resetting the session continues to work as before and correctly controls the audio element.
No changes are made to the Enhanced Breathing page background audio behavior (it must still load from "/assets/breathing/ambient.mp3").

constraints: Frontend immutable paths must not be edited (frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, and frontend/src/components/ui/*).
Do not change the Enhanced Breathing background audio path "/assets/breathing/ambient.mp3".
nonGoals: Adding third-party audio hosting integrations, authentication, or API keys.
Implementing text-to-speech or a generated voiceover for the meditation script.
Changing backend canister APIs or data models for audio playback.
